I’ll run the inverse design with the default 3DCP search space and required OPC, then check the candidate mixes against the same wall geometry and schedule.
**The default OPC-required search found no feasible mix for this wall.** It screened **4,096 mixes**; returned candidates came from relaxed screening and all failed the physical buildability check.

The highest buildability-ranked candidate is an **experimental starting point only**:

| Component or ratio | Candidate |
|---|---:|
| OPC / limestone powder, binder mass fractions | 0.78 / 0.22 |
| w/b | 0.338 |
| s/b | 1.13 |
| PCE superplasticiser, % of binder mass | 1.42% |

Its predicted initial static yield stress is **351 [19, 10,179] Pa**, reported as q50 [q10, q90]. The physical calculation indicates plastic collapse around **36 mm**. Required layer cycle time is **≥474 s**, versus **≤75 s** allowed by open time.

The run retained **12.5 mm** layers, **29.61 mm** filament width, **60 s** cycles, and free-wall buckling checks.

Published evidence offers a stronger starting point for laboratory trials: [BFS60](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jobe.2025.112841) used **0.40 OPC / 0.60 GGBFS**, **w/b 0.30**, **s/b 1.15**, **PCE 0.47%**, and **VMA 0.14%**, with reported static yield measurements of **12,800 and 35,400 Pa**. Measurement timing and VMA identity need checking before replication; this does not establish suitability for your wall.

**Recommendation:** address buckling with bracing, wall returns, or greater thickness before further mix optimization. Structuration predictions provide order-of-magnitude guidance; final selection needs experimental verification.

input.markdown:
# Wall buildability assessment and mix design

## Job and assumptions
User inputs: 600 mm high, 1,500 mm long straight wall, two filaments, 25 mm nozzle, 50 mm/s, 60 min open time. Supplied material: initial static yield stress 3,000 Pa and Athix 1 Pa/s.

Calculator defaults: 12.5 mm layer height, 29.61 mm filament width, 48 layers, 60 s layer cycle, zero dwell and immediate printing start. Density 2,100 kg/m³, safety factor 1.5, and E/tau = 25; free-wall buckling enabled. Total printing time: 48 min.

## Assessment
**Non-printable as a free-standing straight wall; elastic buckling governs.**
- Buckling limit: layer 17, approximately 212.5 mm.
- Plastic-collapse limit without safety factor: approximately 423 mm; safety-factor-adjusted layer capacity: 18.403512.
- Open time passes, but no feasible cycle-time window exists: minimum 160.512367 s for plastic stability with safety factor versus maximum 75 s for open time.
- At the current cycle, plastic stability requires initial static yield stress 7,824.593606 Pa with Athix fixed at 1 Pa/s, or Athix 2.675206 Pa/s with initial yield stress fixed at 3,000 Pa. These are alternative plastic-stability thresholds, not buckling solutions.

## Default OPC-required design
The default search screened 4,096 mixes and found zero feasible mixes under the original screening constraints. Candidates returned after relaxed screening all failed the physical buildability check. No mix is recommended for the unchanged job.

Highest buildability-ranked relaxed candidate (experimental starting point only):
| Parameter | Value |
|---|---:|
| portland_cement, binder mass fraction | 0.78 |
| limestone_powder, binder mass fraction | 0.22 |
| w/b | 0.338 |
| s/b | 1.13 |
| superplasticiser_pce, % of binder mass, product basis | 1.42 |
| Initial static yield stress, q50 [q10, q90], Pa | 351 [19, 10179] |
| Plastic-collapse height, mm | approximately 36 |
| Minimum cycle time, s | 474 |
| Maximum cycle time from open time, s | 75 |

Composition values above are the tool's rounded candidate summary. The design uses predicted fresh properties rather than the supplied material measurements. Structuration predictions are weak-model, order-of-magnitude guidance; published measurements are the primary evidence for choosing trial formulations. The returned inline summary did not expose a training-range violation count, so absence of extrapolation has not been established.

## Published trial analogue
BFS60, “Effect of fly ash and blast furnace slag on 3D printable concrete”:
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jobe.2025.112841

Reported composition: OPC 0.40 / GGBFS 0.60, w/b 0.30, s/b 1.15, PCE 0.47% and VMA 0.14% of binder. Retrieved static yield-stress measurements: 12,800 and 35,400 Pa. These are separate reported measurements, not a prediction interval; measurement timing/protocol and VMA identity require checking. This analogue is not a validated solution for the specified wall and was retrieved separately from the default search.

## Action
Add bracing, returns, a closed path, or greater wall thickness to address buckling, then reassess plastic stability and open time. Slowing alone does not resolve the present incompatible cycle-time limits. Consider accelerator/VMA adjustments or lower w/b only with extrusion, open-time, and interlayer checks. Measure fresh stiffness and structuration and conduct trial printing. Literature-trained correlations and simplified physical calculations do not replace experimental verification.
